summary: The article promotes 'Greens in the City', a public health campaign led by Dr. Angela Patterson following the Community Health Summit on September 15, 2023, to improve eating habits in urban communities. It covers grassroots gardens and cooking classes, zoning and tax policy for food deserts, the Fresh Find app, nutrition education, philanthropic investment, and communal meals. It closes with a vision of edible urban landscapes built through community collaboration.
one_line: The 'Greens in the City' campaign mobilizes gardens, policy, tech, education, funding and community meals to promote healthier eating in urban areas.
key_facts: The Community Health Summit was held on September 15, 2023, and led to a new public health campaign on urban dietary habits.
Dr. Angela Patterson spearheaded the initiative named 'Greens in the City'.
'Greens in the City' includes community gardens in vacant lots, farmers' markets with local produce, and 'from scratch' cooking classes in neighborhood centers.
Marcus Johnson, a local restaurateur, converted part of his eatery into a communal space teaching budget-friendly, nutrient-packed meals.
As of October 3, 2023, Councilwoman Sofia Rodriguez has been pioneering zoning laws to attract grocery stores to food deserts and offering tax breaks and subsidies for stocking fresh produce.
A citywide initiative backed by Sofia Rodriguez aims to revamp student school lunches by January 2024.
The 'Fresh Find' app, created by Jasmine Lee, rolled out on November 21, 2023, and geo-locates the nearest sources of healthy food while providing discounts.
Dietician Emily Torres has held public seminars since September 22, 2023, on dissecting food labels and debunking diet myths.
As of December 8, 2023, Calvin Hughes's foundation has pledged hefty donations to urban farming projects.
Calvin Hughes said: "Every dollar we put into these programs is a future savings bond for our city's health fund."
The 'Sunday Suppers' began on October 15, 2023, at the Franklin Community Center, where families share meals and swap recipes.
Food deserts are defined as areas with limited access to affordable and nutritious food.
Cited economic benefits of better nutrition include reduced healthcare costs, increased workforce productivity, and local health and wellness jobs.
